verses.uthmani: أَلَمْ تَرَ كَيْفَ فَعَلَ رَبُّكَ بِأَصْحَٰبِ ٱلْفِيلِ
verses.indopak: اَلَمۡ تَرَ كَيۡفَ فَعَلَ رَبُّكَ بِاَصۡحٰبِ الۡفِيۡلِ ؕ
verses.transliteration: Alam tara kaifa fa'ala rabbuka bi ashaabil feel
verses.saheeh: Have you not considered, [O Muhammad], how your Lord dealt with the companions of the elephant?
verses.khattab: Have you not seen ˹O Prophet˺ how your Lord dealt with the Army of the Elephant
verses.jalalayn: Have you not considered (an interrogative meant to provoke marvel, in other words, ‘marvel at’) the way in which your Lord dealt with the Men of the Elephant?, who was named Mahmūd, and the men were Abraha, King of Yemen and his troops. He had built a church in San‘ā’ in order to divert pilgrims away from Mecca to it. A man from among the Banū Kināna defecated in it and stained its prayer niche with a deflowered virgin’s blood, in contempt of it. Abraha then swore that he would knock down the Ka‘ba. So he approached Mecca with his troops riding Yemeni elephants with Mahmūd at the vanguard. But when they turned to destroy the Ka‘ba, God unleashed upon them what He relates in His words:
verses.romanUrdu: Tumne dekha nahin ke tumhare Rubb ne haathi walon ke saath kya kiya

verses.transliteration: Alam yaj'al kai dahum fee tad leel
verses.saheeh: Did He not make their plan into misguidance?
verses.khattab: Did He not frustrate their scheme
verses.jalalayn: Did He not make — that is to say, He did [indeed] make — their stratagem, to destroy the Ka‘ba, go astray, [ending up] in failure and destruction,
verses.romanUrdu: Kya usne unki tadbir ko akarat nahin kar diya

verses.saheeh: And He sent against them birds in flocks,
verses.khattab: For He sent against them flocks of birds
verses.jalalayn: and unleashed upon them swarms of birds, [birds] in droves, one following the next (it is said there is no singular form for it [abābīl], like asātīr; but some say that the singular is abūl or ibāl or ibbīl, similar [in constructed pattern] to ‘ajūl, miftāh and sikkīn),
verses.romanUrdu: Aur un par parindo ke jhund ke jhund bhej diye

verses.transliteration: Tar meehim bi hi jaaratim min sij jeel
verses.saheeh: Striking them with stones of hard clay,
verses.khattab: that pelted them with stones of baked clay
verses.jalalayn: pelting them with stones of baked clay,
verses.romanUrdu: Jo un par pakey huey mitti ke patthar phenk rahey thay

verses.saheeh: And He made them like eaten straw.
verses.khattab: leaving them like chewed up straw
verses.jalalayn: thus making them like devoured blades?, like the leaves of crops which have been consumed, trampled and destroyed by animals. God destroyed each one of them with his own stone, inscribed with his name, larger than a lentil [in size] but smaller than a chick-pea, able to pierce through an egg, a man, or an elephant and go through the ground. This took place in the year of the Prophet’s birth (s).
verses.romanUrdu: Phir un ka yeh haal kar diya jaise janwaron ka khaya hua bhoosa
